dependencies.reason: builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation
reads the effective setting protected_branches, whose key that package registers, and matches it with the one branch-glob matcher of the repository in internal/workspace/branchglob.go
keeps the origin head of every branch current as the ref refs/remotes/origin/<name>, which is the lease of a forced push, and provides the sync route the second execution path uses
emits its hub events through the event log component

tasks.title: Serve the push route and push a branch fast-forward
steps: Add the behaviours of the push request and of the fast-forward push to internal/gitrepo/push_test.go and internal/workspace/push_test.go and confirm they fail

Extend the test origin of package 10 in internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest, the one test origin of the repository, with a mode (SmartOrigin) that serves a bare repository through `git http-backend` with pushes enabled, over TLS, with optional Basic authentication, a request counter and a way to read a branch head; keep the existing read-only mode working

Add a push operation to internal/gitrepo that takes the copy, the origin URL, the resolved credential, a commit id, a branch name and a context, and runs one `git push` in machine-readable mode with the single refspec `<commit>:refs/heads/<name>`; it never pushes tags or other branches, never prompts, and hands the credential to `git` the way the clone of package 10 does (not in the URL, the arguments or the copy's configuration)
Make the operation return a result of pushed or up_to_date from the per-ref status git reports, and a typed non-fast-forward error when git refuses the ref as non-fast-forward or fetch-first

Register POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/branches/{name}/push on the hub's router with scope `workspaces:write` and the write need of the workspace access rule; take the branch name from the router's once-decoded path value
Parse the body: none, empty and `{}` mean force false; unknown members are ignored; anything that is not a JSON object, or a `force` that is not a JSON boolean (null included), is 400 invalid_request
Validate the decoded name with the branch-name rule of package 10 and answer 400 invalid_request when it fails
Build the handler from its collaborators as parameters (workspace store, credential resolver, push operation, event writer, push deadline) so that tests can replace the push operation with a stub

Read the head of refs/heads/<name> once, resolve the origin credential from the workspace's secrets for this call, run the push operation and answer 200 with branch, sha, remote `origin`, remote_url and result

Answer 409 non_fast_forward for the typed error, with a message that names the recorded origin head of the branch, read with OriginHead of internal/gitrepo (the ref refs/remotes/origin/<name> of the hub's copy), when that ref exists, and says to sync or to push with force
Wire the handler on the composition value of internal/hub (package 03) so that a running parleyd serves the route

tasks.title: Refuse pushes by workspace state and branch kind
steps: Add the refusal behaviours and the order table to internal/workspace/push_test.go and confirm they fail
After the body and the branch name, ask the state guard of package 10 about the addressed workspace and return its 409 answer
Refuse a workspace of kind fork with 400 fork_has_no_origin, whatever the state of its parent
On a carry-patch workspace refuse the branch equal to the record's `integration_branch` with 403 integration_branch; a null `integration_branch` refuses nothing

Declare the patch-branch lookup as an interface in internal/workspace, PatchBranchLookup (given a workspace slug and a branch, whether the branch is the branch of a registered, non-deleted patch, or an error), with the registration function RegisterPatchBranchLookup; package 31 implements and registers it, and this package registers none. With none registered no branch is a patch branch; when it reports a registered, non-deleted patch refuse with 403 patch_branch; when it returns an error answer 503 unavailable

Match branch globs only with MatchAnyBranchGlob of internal/workspace/branchglob.go, the one matcher of the repository, which package 11 delivers; add no matcher and no glob test table of the matcher here

Read the workspace's protected globs as the effective `protected_branches` setting, through EffectiveSettings of the settings registry (the key and its default, the default branch alone, are package 11's); refuse with 403 protected_branch when force is true and a glob matches
Answer 404 branch_not_found when refs/heads/<name> does not exist in the hub's copy, as the last check before the push
Keep the order body, branch name, status, fork, integration branch or patch branch, forced protected branch, branch exists; none of these refusals contacts origin

tasks.title: Force a push only under a lease
steps: Add the forced-push behaviours to internal/gitrepo/push_test.go and internal/workspace/push_test.go and confirm they fail

Extend the push operation with a lease argument: either a commit id origin's branch must still have, or the statement that origin must not have the branch; with a lease the operation passes git an explicit force-with-lease for that one ref and never a plain force

Return the result forced when git reports a forced update, pushed for a fast-forward or a new branch, up_to_date when origin's branch already equals the commit, and a typed lease error when git refuses the ref because the lease is stale
In the handler, when force is true, read the recorded origin head of the branch with OriginHead of internal/gitrepo and pass it as the lease, or pass must-not-exist when none is recorded
Answer 409 origin_moved for the typed lease error and leave the recorded origin head untouched

tasks.title: Classify the failures of a push and enforce its deadline
steps: Add the failure table, the timeout and the unreadable-credential behaviours to internal/workspace/push_test.go and internal/gitrepo/push_test.go and confirm they fail

Extend the test origin with switches: answer a fixed HTTP status to the push, refuse every update from a server-side hook with a given text, stall after accepting the connection, close its listener, and serve a certificate the hub does not trust

Make the push operation return a typed error for each class: rejected by origin for the ref (with origin's reason), unauthenticated, forbidden, not found, unreachable (name resolution, connection, TLS) and other; read the class from the per-ref status when git reports one and from the transport failure otherwise, for HTTPS origins and for the messages of the SSH transport

Map the classes to 422 origin_rejected, 502 origin_unauthenticated, 502 origin_forbidden, 502 origin_not_found, 502 origin_unreachable and 502 upstream_error; for origin_unauthenticated say in the message whether the workspace has no credential or origin rejected the stored one
Run the push under the handler's deadline (2 minutes in production, a parameter in tests); when it passes, end the `git` process and its children, wait for them, and answer 504 origin_timeout
When the credential resolver returns an error, answer 500 internal without calling the push operation
Return every failure as an error value; the push operation never ends the process and leaves no temporary file or child process behind on any outcome

tasks.title: Record the origin head and the push event, also for a caller that left
steps: Add the record, event and disconnect behaviours to internal/workspace/push_test.go and confirm they fail

After a result of pushed, forced or up_to_date, set refs/remotes/origin/<name> of the hub's copy to the pushed commit with SetOriginHead of internal/gitrepo, remembering the value it had, then write the `parley.workspace.push` event and, for the default branch, the workspace's `origin_head_sha` in one store transaction
After a failure of the push itself, write the event alone, with ok false and the answer's error_type, and leave the origin head as it was
Fill the event: workspace the slug, the caller as actor, resource_type `branch`, resource_id the branch name, metadata branch, sha, force, ok, remote_url and either result or error_type, never both
Write no event for a request refused before the push or ended by an unreadable credential

Run the push and the writes after it on a context that is not cancelled when the request's connection closes, bounded by the push deadline, so that a caller that disconnects changes neither the outcome nor the records
When the transaction after an accepted push fails, put refs/remotes/origin/<name> back to the remembered value (delete it when it did not exist) and answer 500 internal

tasks.title: Scrub every message of the push route
steps: Add the scrubbing behaviours to internal/workspace/push_test.go and confirm they fail

Pass every error message of the route and every text written into the event through the scrubber of internal/scrub, giving it the token or password of the credential resolved for this push as a secret to replace
Rely on the scrubber's cut so that no message exceeds 1024 characters and none ends inside a multi-byte character
Compute remote_url once per request as the workspace's git_url with URL userinfo removed (a `git@host:path` origin is given unchanged) and use that value in the answer and in the event

tasks.title: Add the `parley workspace push` command
steps: Add the command's behaviours to internal/cli/workspace_test.go and confirm they fail
Add `push <slug> <branch>` to the workspace command group with the boolean flag `--force`; any other number of arguments is a usage error through the CLI's own error path, with nothing sent
With `--force`, write one warning line to stderr that origin's branch may be replaced, before the request is sent

Send POST /workspaces/<slug>/branches/<branch>/push through the CLI's HTTP client, which percent-encodes each argument as one path segment, with the body {"force": false} or {"force": true} and a request timeout of 3 minutes
Print the hub's answer through the CLI's output function; a hub error and its exit status are left to the CLI's shared error handling
Add the end-to-end tests of both execution paths to test/e2e/workspace_push_test.go: the developer's push from the shell and the forced push stopped by the lease and repeated after a sync
